name: Ten
why: 1: only 10 (J). The 0 cannot stand alone, so it must join the digit before it.

name: Two zeros
why: 0: 10 uses the first 0, and the second 0 cannot stand alone or make 00.

name: Too big to pair
why: 1: 27 is not a letter, so only 2 7 (BG).

name: A leading zero
why: 0: 06 is not a letter; only 1 to 26 without a leading zero.

name: Zeros inside
why: 3: the 0 forces 20, which forces 1 to stand alone; then 1 2 3 4 can be read as 1 2 3 4, 12 3 4 or 1 23 4.

name: Forty ones
why: 165,580,141. Plain recursion makes about that many calls (the counts follow the Fibonacci numbers), which is too slow. Each position needs only two earlier answers.

name: 100,000 digits
why: The count is a number with thousands of digits, so return it modulo 1,000,000,007. Memoised recursion fails here: this input needs far more nested calls than Python allows (about 1,000, and only a few hundred with functools.cache in the browser). Fill a table with a loop instead (lesson 3).

name: A bad zero near the end
why: 0: the 0 after a 3 cannot be read in any way, so there are no decodings at all, however many there were before it.
